question: What protection is stated for one bitten by great serpents, with respect to poison entering the body?
premises: A person may be bitten by great serpents.
Even in that condition, poison does not enter the body.
The negation applies to the action of poison entering.
inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
uncertainties: Basis of this protection not specified in this verse
plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
